page0.text:
"..."
I open my eyes.
My eyes are not the only thing that wake up, as my sleeping mind wakes up as well.

page1.text:
"The wound is... Not a problem."
I check the wound on my left shoulder.
It still hurts, but there's no intense pain like last night.
The heat in my body has gone down as well.
It shouldn't be a problem for me to move around.

page2.text:
I eat breakfast and fill my empty stomach.
Food comes before anything. My body won't move how I want it to unless it gets the nutrition it needs.

page3.text:
"...All right."
I reapply the bandage on my left shoulder.
My exposed skin and wound have turned dark blue.
My wound hasn't healed up, and I can see dark red skin peeking through.

page4.text:
"...Of course. Saber's not here right now."
I disinfect for my peace of mind, put gauze over it, and wrap bandages around it.
Wrapping bandages and constricting the wound is the most primitive first-aid treatment, but I have to do this or my wound would expand just by moving my left arm.
"All done. I just need a weapon now."

page5.text:
The sky is cloudy.
It must be really cold today, as there's still frost left in the yard.

page6.text:
...
But, this has nothing to do with me.
I don't feel any cold.
My body is so hot I want to pour ice water over my head.
Even then, my body is in much better condition compared to yesterday.

page7.text:
These bamboo swords are the only things that I could use as weapons after all.
I choose the one that seems like it could pass magical energy through it the best and wrap it in my bag.

page8.text:
Then, I slap my cheeks.
I don't know if it was to psyche myself up again or if I was preparing to never come back here.
I don't know why I did it myself.

page9.text:
I sling the bag over my right shoulder and head outside.
The place where I've spent many years.
I didn't even look back at the shed that could be considered my own room.
